name: IKI Medium Grants

funder.name: German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN)

administered_by.name: IKI Office at Zukunft - Umwelt - Gesellschaft (ZUG) gGmbH

summary: Annual ideas competition of Germany's International Climate Initiative for non-profit organisations established in Germany that run two- to three-year climate and biodiversity projects with one or two local partners in developing and emerging countries.
reporting: Grantees submit an annual interim report by 30 April (progress statement with results and IKI standard indicators, plus a financial statement) and a yearly update on project results to the IKI Office.

eligibility.rule: Is based in Germany or another EU Member State when submitting the outline
Has an independent German branch with its own management and accounting before first payment
Has 3 years of international cooperation and 3 years of experience in the chosen thematic area
Can independently plan, implement and manage project finances
Is not a government body, private company or one-person company, except an independent think tank with public analyses
Average annual request is at most 50% of average annual revenue over the last 2 years

documents: Reference projects of the implementing organisation (Annex 1)
Reference projects of each implementing partner (Annex 2)
Evidence of non-profit tax status, for non-profit enterprises

opens.quote: The ideas competition (call) opens on 13 October 2026 and closes on 12 January 2027 at 11.59 am (CET).

deadline.quote: The ideas competition (call) opens on 13 October 2026 and closes on 12 January 2027 at 11.59 am (CET).

deadline.text: The deadline for the submission of project outlines was 20 January 2026.

status.quote: The projects for the sixth IKI Medium Grants Funding Call have been selected following a comprehensive assessment process and selection discussions involving the responsible reviewers and the relevant ministries.

deadline.quote: The deadline for the submission of project outlines was 20 January 2026.

administered_by.quote: Once the IKI Office at Zukunft - Umwelt - Gesellschaft gGmbH (ZUG) has reviewed the detailed project proposal, a final decision will be made as to funding.

applicant_types.quote: Who receives funding? Non-profit organisations and companies with a permanent business establishment, branch, or other facility serving the activities of the grant recipient in Germany at the time of the first disbursement of a grant awarded.

geography.quote: The IKI supports projects that contribute to the implementation of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change and the Convention on Biological Diversity in developing and emerging economies.

places.quote: A country must be ODA-eligible by the deadline for submitting the project outline. More information on ODA eligibility can be found on the DAC list of ODA recipients.

access.quote: In the first phase (outline phase), interested implementing organisations are invited to submit project outlines within the framework of an ideas competition.

window.quote: How often is funding provided? Annual selection procedure

amount.quote: The volume of finance provided to each project by the IKI Medium Grants can vary between EUR 300,000 and EUR 800,000.

co_finance_required.quote: The grant recipients must make an appropriate contribution to the financing of the purpose to be funded with their own funding, taking into account their financial strength.

consortium_required.quote: These organisations must enter into a partnership with one or two local implementing organisations based in the implementing country or region.

reporting.quote: Therefore, all IKI implementing organisations must submit an annual report on the progress of their project referred to as interim reports.

effort.quote: The deadline for timely and complete submission is 12 January 2027 at 11:59 CET
The project outlines consist of the completed form and a project concept. The assessment is carried out in several stages: First, compliance with the formal requirements is checked.
Only selected outlines will be invited to submit a complete, formal project proposal by means of the “Request for Project Proposal”.

eligibility.quote: At that stage, the lead organisation must be based in Germany or another EU Member State.
Before the first disbursement of funding, however, the lead organisation must have a permanent, independently operating branch in Germany with its own management and accounting.

During the outline phase, the implementing organisation must demonstrate three years of experience in international co-operation through the attached reference projects as well as three years of experience in the selected thematic funding area.
the ability to independently plan, implement, and manage the finances of their projects

Government bodies, private-sector companies, and one-person companies are not eligible for funding. An exception applies to think tanks, provided that they can demonstrate their independence and make their analyses transparent and publicly available.
The average funding volume per fiscal year is not allowed to exceed 50% of the average annual turnover of the applicant over the last two years.

after_award.quote: all IKI implementing organisations must submit an annual report on the progress of their project referred to as interim reports.

documents.quote: The project outlines consist of the completed form and a project concept.
